questions.text: What are you quietly proud of that nobody ever congratulates you for?
What's the biggest way you've changed in the last five years — and did you choose it or did it happen to you?
What good advice do you regularly give and completely fail to follow yourself?
What used to be hard for you that's now completely automatic?
What belief have you outgrown, and what replaced it?
What drains your energy fastest, and what refills it?
What's a compliment you received years ago that you still think about?
What's something you were afraid of that you did anyway? How did it go?
Describe a genuinely good ordinary day for you, start to finish. No holidays, no big events.
What do you spend the most time on that you'd cut if you could, and what's stopping you?
What are you waiting for permission to do? Who exactly are you waiting on?
What about your current life would your younger self be most impressed by?
What would your younger self give you grief about? Are they right?
What do you need to start saying no to?
What are you actively working on about yourself right now, and how's it going honestly?
What's a piece of luck that shaped your life more than any of your decisions did?
What's the hardest thing you've had to learn, and did you have to learn it more than once?
What have you forgiven yourself for, and how long did that take?
When you're running on empty, what actually works — and what do you do instead?
What question do you hate being asked, and why does it land badly?
What used to matter enormously to you and now barely registers?
What do you want to be known for by the people who actually know you?
What's the best decision you've made that seemed small at the time?
What are you stubborn about, and is it serving you?
Who do you compare yourself to, and is that comparison fair to either of you?
What were you completely certain about and completely wrong about?
What conversation are you putting off? You don't have to name names.
What do you actually need more of right now — rest, challenge, company, quiet?
Where are your standards for yourself higher than your standards for everyone else?
How good are you at asking for help, and where did that come from?
What's one small thing that went right for you today? It counts.
What one thing of yours would you want to end up with someone who'd appreciate it?
What actually motivates you — not what you'd put on a form. The real one.
What boundary did you have to learn the hard way to set?
What are you good at that doesn't feel like an achievement because it's easy for you?
What would you pick back up if you stopped worrying about being bad at it?
What period of your life were you happiest in, and what made it work?
What path did you nearly take? Do you ever wonder about that version of you?
What got you through your hardest stretch — a person, a habit, or sheer stubbornness?
Name something specific you're grateful for today. Not the big obvious one — a small one.
What value did you inherit from your family that you've kept on purpose?
What did you grow up around that you deliberately chose not to carry forward?
